---
title: "Research"
description: "TIDE Lab's research themes and emerging programme."
---

TIDE Lab develops research at the intersection of four broad themes. Economics provides our shared analytical framework. The agenda below is an initial structure; individual project pages will document specific questions, methods, collaborators, outputs, and status as projects are launched.

## Technology and work

We study how new technologies affect firms, workers, skills, productivity, and the distribution of economic opportunity. This theme includes both adoption decisions and the adjustment processes that follow technological change.

## Immigration and mobility

We examine why people move, how migrants integrate into destination economies, and how mobility affects workers, firms, households, and local labour markets in both origin and destination regions.

## Demographic transitions

Our demographic research considers population ageing, fertility, family formation, and intergenerational change, with particular attention to their implications for labour supply, public finance, and economic growth.

## Education and human capital

We study how education shapes skills, economic mobility, and opportunity across generations. This theme includes educational access and attainment, human-capital formation, and the links between education, technology, migration, and demographic change.

Across all four themes, we ask how institutions and public policy shape adaptation, distributional outcomes, and social welfare. Our approach combines economic reasoning with transparent empirical analysis.
